newsitem.title: USA: Containerboard hit Tenneco's Q1 oper income.
newsitem.headline: Containerboard hit Tenneco's Q1 oper income.

text.p: Tenneco Inc said Tuesday that although its Automotive division set first quarter records in revenues and operating income, Tenneco Packaging reported a decline in operating income due largely to weaker containerboard prices.

Tenneco Automotive had operating income of $80 million compared with $59 million in the prior year quarter. Tenneco Packaging had operating income of $80 million, including a pre-tax gain of $38 million from lease refinancing. In the first quarter last year, Tenneco Packaging had operating income of $106 million.

Tenneco said the ongoing operating income benefit from the lease financing is expected to be about $15 million annually. The cash flow improvement is projected to be more than $120 million over the first two years and about $250 million over the next five years, due to lower lease costs and other benefits, Tenneco said.
First quarter specialty packaging operating income was up 11 percent, led by contributions from the foam products acquisition and stronger volume growth, the company said.

"We are pleased by the record results in our automotive parts business and the continued solid performance of our specialty packaging operations in the first quarter," said Tenneco Chairman Dana Mead.

"While the containerboard market remains disappointingly weak, we continue to make steady progress in offsetting the cyclicality in that business by growing our highly profitable specialty and protective packaging operations. At the same time, with our recently announced Automotive reorganization, we are on target in our program to lower corporate overhead in the range of $100 million by early 1998," Mead said.
Tenneco posted operating earnings of $0.44 a share, up from $0.34 cents a year-ago. Net income from continuing operations rose 27 percent to $76 million, up from $60 million a year ago.
Containerboard mill cost reductions and productivity improvements continue to be a primary focus, with a two-year target of $75 million in cost reductions, Tenneco said.
More than half is expected to be realized in 1997. On an annual basis these improvements will reduce containerboard costs by more than $30 per ton, the company said.
"While we are not satisfied with containerboard results in the quarter, we have fared better than most of our competitors, and we are well positioned for any upturn in pricing," Mead said.

"At the same time, the outlook for specialty packaging is highly encouraging. We continue to introduce products for the faster growing markets, such as convenience food and agricultural packaging, which should continue to boost sales and improve our operating margins."

Tenneco said its new structure has allowed it improve customer focus, enhance global competitiveness and reduce overhead costs. This corporate effort is expected to yield about $100 million in cost reductions by early 1998, the company said.
During 1997, Tenneco plans to further reduce working capital on a percentage of revenues basis, generating the equivalent of an additional $230 million in cash flow.

The company's three-year working capital initiative begun in early 1996 has already reduced working capital on a percentage-of-revenues basis by 4.5 percentage points, which is equivalent to a $280 million increase in cash flow.
